newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell 45 pct stake in oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell 45 pct stake in oil refinery.

text.p: Ukraine will sell a 45 percent stake in AT Lisichansknaftorsyntez, the country's second-largest oil refinery, to a strategic investor, a senior government official said on Friday.
"The government has accepted a resolution to sell 45 percent of shares, and the government will keep 51 percent," Anatoly Mynchenko, state minister in charge of the industrial sector, told Reuters.
Mynchenko did not say what the State Property Fund, which is responsible for privatisation, would do with 24.6 percent of the refinery's shares, distributed to refinery workers last year.

Investor obligations would include restructuring the refinery's $70 million debt to a German bank, bringing output to at least six million tonnes of oil annually, and injecting $12 million to modernise the facility, he said.
The refinery has an annual capacity of 16 million tonnes and is located 500 km east of Kiev.

The Lisichansk refinery, one of more than 200 enterprises for which the government is seeking strategic investment in order to attract foreign dollars, refined just 1.8 million tonnes of oil for the first 10 months of this year.
A Ukrainian court has delayed bankruptcy hearings into the refinery.

Ukraine's six oil refineries routinely processed 60 million tonnes of crude oil a year in the Soviet era, but they refined only 16.8 million tonnes in 1995, reflecting sharp declines in Russian crude oil supplies.
